correctness.rationale: Each cell integral of (I−P)f vanishes, so no contribution propagates between cells. On each cell the constant is killed and normalized nonconstant cosines are mapped into the complete sine basis with coefficients h/(mπ). This gives every positive singular value and its multiplicity, and compactness. For t>0 the number strictly above t on cell j is q_j=ceil(h_j/(πt))−1, including thresholds exactly on a ladder. Taking t=s_k yields 1=Σh_j≤πt(N+Σq_j)≤πt(N+k−1). Equality requires both Σq_j=k−1 and equality on each cell separately; conversely every positive composition of N+k−1 yields exactly k−1 values above the threshold and one value at it from every cell. This proves attainment and rules out any other ordered mesh. The uniform value 1/[πN ceil(k/N)] gives the asserted congruence including N=1, and the k=2 examples increase the operator norm for N≥2. Summation of the complete ladders gives divergence for 0<p≤1 and the stated zeta formula for p>1; strict convexity gives the unique global minimizer. The exact-rational checker was inspected without execution; its finite ranks and grids do not prove the all-rank optimization.

evidence: Wang considers minimizing sums of first component eigenvalues. Tavares–Zilio consider monotone functionals of prescribed lists of component eigenvalues. The Resultary affine-spline record gives derivative-seminorm H/(2π) approximation and width optimality for 2N dimensions.
broader_coverage.reasoning: An increasing eigenvalue minimization or fixed width bound is not maximization of a variable-index order statistic on the pooled spectrum. The catalogue Sobolev record also uses a different projector. Those conclusions do not give the present converse at equality.

evidence: The standard one-interval Sobolev formula gives each ladder. In the equivalent Dirichlet problem, variational interlacing gives a bound but does not identify which placements realize it; the frozen proof's joint ceiling inequality forces all cells simultaneously to hit the same threshold at equality.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The optimization is not a parameter substitution into a prior width or sum/max partition theorem. It needs the discrete allocation of ranks across all component spectra and both directions of the attainment/rigidity statement. The closest accessible prior comparisons establish ingredients and neighboring objectives, not the final combined-spectrum claim.

evidence: Edmunds–Lang give the p=2 embedding relation a_k=λ_k^(−1/2) and the one-interval first-derivative ladder. In the frozen claim the equivalent objective is maximizing the kth Dirichlet eigenvalue of the disjoint union with internal Dirichlet nodes; its optimum is the (N+k−1)st whole-interval eigenvalue.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The equivalence is exact, not a claim of a novel local spectral calculation. Removing N−1 node constraints restores the whole-interval space and interlacing bounds the optimal value from above; it does not by itself show attainment and characterize all maximizing meshes. The equality analysis identifies the allowable nodes as subsets of the whole-interval nodal grid. No equivalent prior exact equality law was established by the bounded checks.

value.rationale: Mesh design for a target singular rank is a natural objective distinct from minimizing total error or the worst-case norm. The exact equality set answers which meshes improve a desired index and when a uniform mesh is already optimal. The all-index quantization, attained rigidity and explicit second-rank tradeoff are the useful content, rather than calculating the classical one-cell eigenvalues again.
